newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - The banks are back.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - The banks are back.

text.p: A number of Brazilian banks are lining up to issue Eurobonds in a week that could see more than $500 million in fresh corporate paper, traders and analysts said.
THE PRIMARY MARKET was expected to be visited by:

* Unibanco - a two tranche deal totalling $300 million through lead manager Morgan Stanley. The first tranche will be a $200 million three-year bond, seen pricing at a spread of 160-170 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
The other tranche is a $100 million six-year bond tipped to come at a 200-220 bp spread.
* Dutch bank Rabobank's Brazil unit was seen pricing a $100 million three-year bond through ABN Amro. The deal was seen coming at a spread of about 150 bp.
* Investment bank Pactual is expected to price at least $50 million in five-year bonds through Credit Lyonnais. The bonds were seen coming at a spread of 310-330 bp.

The continued strong presence of Brazilian banks in the market was attributed to new rules allowing banks to park funds raised overseas in dollar-linked, high-yielding domestic securities before loaning the money in Brazi.
Before the new rules, money raised abroad by banks had to be loaned right away or deposited in the Central Bank.
Brazilian banks issued 10 separate Eurobonds in July, amounting to about $875 million.
NON-BANK DEALS SCHEDULED THIS WEEK INCLUDE:

* Abril, the communciations group, was reported pricing a $30-$40 million bond carrying a maturity of three to eight years. Paxton was expected to lead-manage the deal, which could come at a spread of about 330 bp over Treasuries.
Federally owned oil company Petrobras told the financial newspaper Gazeta Mercantil that it would bring its long-awaited 30 billion yen ($250 million) six-year bond to market August 18.
The deal, led by Daiwa Securities, should price at about 190-200 bp over U.S. Treasuries when swapped into dollars.

Meanwhile, state run utility Eletrobras was expected to cancel its $200 million 10-year bond via ABN Amro, which was seen bidding too aggressively for the deal by reportedly promising a spread in the range of 250 bp. The market was expecting the deal to be rebid, but Eletrobras and ABN Amro have not officially commented yet.
IN SECONDARY TRADE, spreads on Brazilian issues tightened by five to 10 bp on average last week as Eurobonds held steady amid falling U.S. Treasury prices, traders said.
High-yielding bonds were the top performers.
CSN's 9.125 percent bond due 2007 ZYJJ tightened to about 305 bp from 335 bp but was still far from its launch price of 275 bp.
Sao Paulo state sewage company Sabesp's 10.0 percent due 2005 tightened to 350 bp after pricing at about 370.
Private electricity company Escelsa, from the state of Espirito Santo, also did well. Escelsa's 10 percent due 2007 narrowed 15 bp to 355 bp, traders said.
((--Sao Paulo Newsroom, 5511 248-5414))
